slides.heading: Find Nodes Distance K
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Find Nodes Distance K, a hard binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Values of all nodes exactly k edges from the node with value `target` (unique values).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Values of all nodes exactly k edges from the node with value target (unique values). Build parent links, then BFS.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Treat the tree as an undirected graph with parent links, then BFS k steps from the target.
slides.narration: Treat the tree as an undirected graph with parent links, then BFS k steps from the target.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Treat as graph: add parent pointers, BFS k levels → O(n)
slides.narration: A tree only lets you go down, but distance can go up too. Recording parents turns it into an undirected graph, and BFS k levels from the target gives the answer in linear time.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Map each node to its parent
3. BFS over left, right and parent
slides.narration: Step by step. First, map each node to its parent. Second, find the target. Third, bFS over left, right and parent. Fourth, collect nodes at distance k.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Target = 3, k = 2: start BFS at 3
slides.narration: We want nodes at distance two from three. First record each node's parent, then BFS from three.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Distance 1: [6, 1]
slides.narration: At distance 1, moving to children and to the parent, we reach 6, 1.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Distance 2: [7, 8, 2]
slides.narration: At distance 2, moving to children and to the parent, we reach 7, 8, 2.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We DFS to build the parent map and locate the target, then BFS k levels, enqueuing unseen children and parent, and return the values in the queue.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Visited set to avoid bouncing back
slides.narration: If k is zero, return the target itself. The seen set stops you from walking back along the same edge.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: There's also a recursive solution without parent maps.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Treat the tree as an undirected graph with parent links, then BFS k steps from the target.
slides.narration: To recap Find Nodes Distance K: Treat the tree as an undirected graph with parent links, then BFS k steps from the target. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
